messages:
maria: Quick experiment results for the reranker bring-up — focusing on query/doc formatting + quantization. TL;DR: int8 hurts some short-query cases (MRR) but NDCG mostly stable; see numbers below.
chris: Which datasets did you run on?
maria: internal-recall-2024 dev (10k q), MS MARCO passages dev subset (5k), and a sampled support-kb set (2k).
devon: What formatting variants did you test?
maria: Tested 4 variants: 
- `title_only`
- `title + \" -- \" + body` (concatenate with separator)
- `query + top3_snippets` (append top-3 retrieved snippets with `<SEP>` tokens)
- `normalized` (lowercase + strip punctuation + collapse whitespace)
Also checked two tokenization modes (whitespace vs sentencepiece).
sophia: Which metrics and eval harness?
maria: MRR@10, NDCG@10, MRR@100 for long-tail. Used our eval script: `python eval/rerank_eval.py --seed 42 --folds 5 --save-outputs`
eval-bot: Job rerank-eval/1751345678 completed :white_check_mark:
maria: Results (MS MARCO dev) — showing float32 vs int8 (MRR@10):
```
format       | float32 MRR@10 | int8 MRR@10 | delta
title_only   | 0.328          | 0.312       | -0.016
title+body   | 0.345          | 0.339       | -0.006
with_snips   | 0.362          | 0.353       | -0.009
normalized   | 0.350          | 0.349       | -0.001
```
chris: And NDCG@10?
maria: NDCG@10 differences are smaller:
```
format       | float32 NDCG@10 | int8 NDCG@10 | delta
title_only   | 0.524           | 0.519        | -0.005
title+body   | 0.538           | 0.536        | -0.002
with_snips   | 0.551           | 0.547        | -0.004
normalized   | 0.545           | 0.545        | 0.000
```
maria: Observations: int8 impact concentrated on very short queries (title_only). Hypothesis: quantization noise changes relative ordering when signal is weak. Tokenizer differences amplified the effect for `normalized` (sentencepiece slightly better).
sophia: Are the deltas statistically significant?
maria: Paired t-test across queries (MS MARCO): title_only p=0.02, with_snips p=0.04, title+body p=0.12, normalized p=0.60. So title_only and with_snips cross sig threshold (p<0.05).
devon: Did you try any fixes (calibration/rescaling)?
maria: Quick experiments: simple temperature scaling on logits (multiplying scores by 0.97) recovered ~0.7 of the MRR gap for title_only. Isotonic regression on dev fold gave similar improvements but needs more data. Example: `scores_cal = scores * 0.97`
chris: How about throughput / memory tradeoffs for int8?
maria: int8 gives ~1.9x throughput and ~2.3x GPU memory reduction on our A100-like nodes. So cost win is real for non-critical routes.
sophia: Recommendations?
maria: For rollout: default to `title+body` formatting for production reranker. If enabling int8, run a small canary (1%) with live traffic and monitor MRR/NDCG via the eval dashboard and query-level regressions. Add an offline check that runs `title_only` subset since it's most sensitive. :mag: :chart_with_upwards_trend:
chris: Anything else to run before we propose this to product?
maria: Add more seeds (ran 3, will expand to 10), expand dataset mix to include multilingual samples, and include retriever+reranker cascade end-to-end eval (reranker-only may hide retriever shift). I'll upload the full outputs to the eval bucket and post link after cleanup.
devon: Thanks — please add the temp-scaling snippet to the experiments repo so infra can wire it for canary toggles.
maria: Will do, filing a follow-up PR: `github.com/redwood/re-ranker/compare/quant-ablation`
